neighborhoods.name: Fagatogo
neighborhoods.description: The downtown and legislative seat of American Samoa, home to the Fono, the courthouse, the market, and the main bus depot on the south shore of Pago Pago Harbor
neighborhoods.character: Downtown, government seat, market town, harborfront, historic

housing.predominantType: Single-family homes and a small stock of walk-up apartments

neighborhoods.character_notes: The most walkable spot on Tutuila: the Fagatogo Market is the hub of the aiga bus system (fares roughly $0.50-$2.00; no buses Sundays), so a retiree here can reach most of the island without a car. Formal rentals are scarce because roughly 90% of land is communally owned under the fa'amatai system and cannot be sold to anyone less than half Samoan, so most housing is family land; expect word-of-mouth listings and lease-only arrangements. LBJ Tropical Medical Center in Faga'alu, the territory's only hospital, is about 5 minutes away by car or bus.

sources.title: Taking the 'Aiga Buses in American Samoa - American Samoa Pocket Guide
Real Property - American Samoa Bar Association

neighborhoods.name: Utulei
neighborhoods.description: Waterfront village on the southwest edge of Pago Pago Harbor housing the governor's office, ASG executive buildings, Utulei Beach Park, and the harbor-area hotels
neighborhoods.character: Waterfront, government offices, hotels, beach park, tidy
neighborhoods.character_notes: The most polished address in the harbor area, with a swimmable beach park, the ASG executive offices, and the Sadie Thompson-linked hotels; what little formal rental stock exists here is often tied to government or contract workers, and it sits at the top of the island's price range. Flat waterfront walking to Fagatogo suits limited mobility better than most of Tutuila, and aiga buses pass along the main road on weekdays. LBJ Tropical Medical Center in Faga'alu is under 10 minutes away; serious care beyond it means a medevac or the roughly 5.5-hour Hawaiian Airlines flight to Honolulu.

neighborhoods.name: Pago Pago Village
neighborhoods.description: Pago Pago village proper sits at the head of the harbor beneath Rainmaker Mountain, a quiet residential settlement that lends its name to the whole capital area
neighborhoods.character: Village life, harbor head, mountain backdrop, rainy, residential
neighborhoods.character_notes: Traditional village life dominates: housing is mostly aiga (extended family) compounds, Sunday is strictly observed with church and quiet, and evening sa (prayer curfew) is respected in some villages — retirees renting here live within that rhythm. This is one of the wettest harbor areas in the Pacific, so expect heavy rain and year-round heat and humidity. Aiga buses run frequently to Fagatogo on weekdays, and LBJ Tropical Medical Center is a short ride around the harbor.

sources.title: Cost of Living in Pago Pago - Wise

neighborhoods.name: Aua & Atu'u
neighborhoods.description: Aua and Atu'u line the north side of Pago Pago Harbor, with Atu'u dominated by the StarKist tuna cannery and Aua a larger traditional village toward Rainmaker Pass
neighborhoods.character: Working harbor, cannery, traditional village, affordable, industrial edge

housing.predominantType: Village family homes; very few formal rentals

neighborhoods.character_notes: The cheapest harbor-area option, but the StarKist cannery in Atu'u brings truck traffic and a fish-processing smell when the wind is wrong, so most retirees would look toward Aua's quieter shoreline. Rental stock is essentially whatever a family compound offers — the communal land system means non-Samoans cannot buy, only lease or rent. Aiga buses run the harbor road to Fagatogo on weekdays; LBJ Tropical Medical Center is about 15 minutes around the harbor.
